slides.title: The big idea
slides.html:
Inscribed Angle Theorem: an inscribed angle (vertex on the circle, sides are chords) measures half its intercepted arc.

Proof, first case: one side is a diameter. If angle ABC has BC a diameter through center O, triangle OAB is isosceles, so angle OBA = angle OAB, and the exterior angle AOC = 2 times angle ABC. The other cases (center inside or outside the angle) add or subtract two of these.

So every inscribed angle that intercepts the same arc has the same measure. A vertex on the other arc intercepts the other arc, and gives the supplement.
